newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ECONOMY IMPROVING ACCORDING TO SURVEY
The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry says its national survey of businesses shows an unmistakable improvement in economic conditions.
The Chamber says while business confidence had been relatively strong since the start of last year, it had not translated into an upturn in economic activity.
The ACCI says its latest survey shows the Australian economy may have turned the corner, with economic activity starting to rise.
It says general business conditions have improved strongly, and only employment growth continues to lag.
The Chamber says static prices and moderate wages growth are part of the reason the economy has begun to turn.
HOWARD NOT CONFIDENT OF AGREED SOLUTION TO WIK IMPASSE
The Prime Minister says he's not confident a negotiated settlement can be reached on legislation to deal with the High Court's Wik ruling that native title and pastoral leases can co-exist.
Mr Howard will hold more talks with interested parties next week, and says he's trying very hard to reach an agreed solution.
The Prime Minister says he respects the High Court's decision, but asserts Parliament has the superior right to change the law if it's in the national interest.
National Party members yesterday called for Federal Parliament to protect farmers' rights, declaring pastoral leases should extinguish native title.
WOODS TO INITIATE DEFAMATION PROCEEDINGS
Lawyers for Senator Bob Woods will commence defamation proceedings today against former lover Roxanne Cameron.
Ms Cameron told the Nine Network's Sixty Minutes program last night, that Senator Woods was dishonest in claiming travel expenses and that he harrassed her.
The Senator has resigned from parliament while police investigate separate claims involving travel expenses.
In a statement last night, he says he'll sue Ms Cameron and Channel Nine in the New South Wales Supreme Court.
The statement denies he harrassed Ms Cameron, and says the public will put its own value on "purchased sensationalism".
CONCERN ABOUT EAR DISEASE IN INDIGENOUS CHILDREN
Concern about ear disease in Aboriginal children has been raised by the Governor-General at an international medical conference in Sydney.
Sir William Deane told the forum something must be done about the problem which has affected 100 per cent of babies born in one Top End community.
The study found the babies developed ear disease by the age of three months, and revealed that half of the primary school children suffered hearing loss.
The Governor-General says in the long term, medical research into the problem could see more effective treatment by vaccination.
But he says in the short term, major improvements would flow from the implementation of known preventative or remedial treatment.
PLASTIC TOPS THE RUBBISH HEAP AFTER CLEAN UP
Plastic was the number one item collected during yesterday's eighth annual Clean Up Australia day.
More than 500,000 volunteers collected an estimated 13,000 tonnes of rubbish during the massive clean up.
Rain washed out efforts in Canberra and Darwin, but the rest of the country was out in force.
Among the rubbish, volunteers found a cache of garden gnomes in Queensland, a BMW car Engine and an empty coffin in New South Wales, and a microwave oven up a tree in Western Australia.
Australian researchers in Antarctica did their bit, while in the New South Wales country town of Dubbo, 640 dumped cars were collected.
MISSING WOMAN'S BODY FOUND
Police have discovered the body of a missing 19-year old Lithgow woman.
Alison Lewis was last seen leaving a hotel in Lithgow's main street early Sunday morning, police say she'd been planning to meet up with friends.
But late yesterday she was found dead at a local sports ground.
Police believe she's been murdered, a post mortem will be conducted on her body today.
CHILDREN CASE TO GO BEFORE COURT TODAY
In New South Wales, the Department of Communnity Services will go to court today over the care of five children, whose mother's whereabouts are unknown.
The five girls, aged between two and 14, were left with relatives and neighbours by their mother late last week.
However the Department last week intervened to take the two eldest children into care, claiming arrangements for their welfare were not satisfactory.
The two teenagers are now staying with child protection agencies, a 10-year-old with her grandmother, and the two youngest with their natural fathers.
A Community Services spokesman says court approval is needed to continue the current arrangements.
CLONCURRY RIVER FLOODING
In the north-west Queensland town of Cloncurry, an emergent situation is expected to stay in place for some time, as emergency services wait for the Cloncurry River to peak.
High rainfalls in the catchment area to the south-west of the town caused the flooding, with the Cloncurry River expected to peak in about eight hours.
A Disaster Co-ordination Centre has been set up in the town to coordinate evacuation efforts.
Police say people have been evacuated from about forty homes in low-lying areas prone to further flooding.
